newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks off 1.73 pct on share forced sale.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks off 1.73 pct on share forced sale.

text.p: Thai stocks fell 1.73 percent by the lunch break as more local investors were forced by margin calls to sell shares to pay off debts, brokers said on Monday.
The SET index declined 17.48 points to a 35-month low of 990.03 on thin 1.1 billion baht by the break. The SET-50 index retreated 1.43 points to 75.03.
"The index fell after investors, mainly locals, were forced to sell shares as they didn't have enough cash to meet maintenance margin calls," said Virat Tippanontakul of First Asia Securities.

The maintenance margin system requires investors to put up cash when related stock prices drop below 25 percent of levels that the shares are originally bought. Investors are forced to sell the shares when prices fall below 15 percent.
"The market mood was bad after the index dipped below the psychological 1,000 level. Selling was seen from small local investors," said Virat.

Brokers said investors remained worried despite denial on rumours last week that some Thai brokerage houses were hit by financial problems of indebted investors failing to meet margin loan obligations.
Brokers said investors were also waried about an upcoming no-confidence debate tabled by the opposition against Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa due to be held on September 18.
General Finance and Securities topped the active list, falling 5.50 baht to 53, Siam Commercial Bank declined 8 to 234 and Electricity Generating slipped 1.50 to 68.
